title: The month onion prices jumped across India
summary: In October 2009, the median onion market moved +72.2% in a month, 6.0 standard deviations from the usual for that month.
why_selected: Chosen automatically: the 6.0σ seasonal move is among the largest on record for onion, across 362 reporting markets.

evidence.observations: monthly medians of daily modal prices; markets need ≥5 reports in both months
caveats: Many market points are district centres, not mandi gates.
Modal prices are reported aggregates, not transaction offers.

scenes.headline: October 2009
scenes.caption: Onion prices across 362 markets that reported in both September 2009 and October 2009.

scenes.headline: Median move +72.2%
scenes.caption: The typical market's onion price jumped 72.2% in one month. 98% of markets moved the same way.

scenes.headline: 6.0× the usual swing
scenes.caption: Compared with the same month in every earlier year on record, this move was 6.0 standard deviations from normal.

scenes.headline: Maharashtra
scenes.caption: Neighbouring markets moved together: the 37 reporting markets in Maharashtra had a median change of +104.7%.

scenes.headline: Panipat
scenes.caption: Panipat (Haryana), one of the busiest markets among the biggest movers: monthly median ₹650 → ₹1,450 per quintal (+123.1%).

scenes.headline: What this does and doesn't show
scenes.caption: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.

conclusion: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.
